historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir's Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Volume 11, Page 163-164. The Ruwaishid were a Jewish tribe who lived in the Arabian Peninsula, particularly in the region of Yemen. They were known for their knowledge of poetry and rhetoric. When the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) sent his emissary, Abdullah bin Ruwaishah, to the Jewish tribe of Banu An-Nadeer, it was Ruwaishid who provided him information about the tribe and its members. This event took place in the 7th century CE, during the early years of Islamic history.
historical_references.context: The Ruwaishid were a Jewish tribe who played a role in early Islamic history by providing information to the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) about the Jewish tribe of Banu An-Nadeer.

historical_references.reference: Al-Maqrizi's Kitab Al-Khitat Wal-Asar, Volume 1, Page 136. The Ruwaishid were a Jewish tribe who lived in the Egyptian town of Tinnis. They were known for their knowledge of the Torah and were considered scholars in Jewish circles. During the Fatimid era, the Ruwaishid had a close relationship with the Fatimid caliphate and provided religious guidance to the caliphs. This relationship lasted until the 11th century CE.
historical_references.context: The Ruwaishid were a Jewish tribe who lived in Egypt and had a close relationship with the Fatimid caliphate, providing religious guidance to the caliphs.
